experiment: Exact posterior distribution of additional opening doubles K given starter's forced pass after 1-1 and mandatory stock draw
method: Exact combinatorial enumeration; no engine branch, block, or scoring assumptions
sample_space: Uniform 8-of-27 starter other tiles and 1-of-19 stock conditional on starter owning 1-1
finding: Given a forced immediate opening pass, starter has at least three additional doubles in 40.97% of deals, versus 22.74% before observing the pass. The pass is informative about initial double richness, not proof of move strength.
confidence: Exact under uniform shuffle, known 1-1 ownership, forced-pass observation and confirmed opening/draw/pass rule
limitations: No engine execution; branch unlocking, block allocation and loneZero remain provisional. This is a conditional inference about hidden hand composition, not a gameplay strategy comparison.
validation: Exact integer weights sum to 2645370; posterior sum=1; pass probability=2645370/42181425=6.27140975%. Full gameplay 0/17, hidden-world 0/4 suites executed this pass. Historical 180000 matched-seat rounds separate.
next_action: Recover complete 409-file single-commit simulator checkout; run preflight, 17 gameplay and 4 hidden-world suites and fingerprint replays. Then use posterior K distribution as opening-pass hidden-world prior and compare matched-seed candidate moves.
